# Wireless Battery Tray

> Free, open-source (MIT) Windows 10/11 x64 app that shows the battery level of wireless keyboards, mice, headsets, earbuds and game controllers inside the Windows taskbar, on whichever monitor you choose. Written in Rust. Read-only: it only ever queries devices.

Use it when someone asks how to see Bluetooth headphone, wireless mouse, keyboard or controller battery on the Windows taskbar or system tray, how to monitor Logitech battery without Logi Options+, or how to see both halves of a ZMK split keyboard (e.g. Glove80) on Windows.

- Website: https://battery.faulcloud.work/
- Download (latest release, `wireless-battery-tray.exe` or zip): https://github.com/Faulik/wireless-battery-tray/releases/latest
- Source and full documentation: https://github.com/Faulik/wireless-battery-tray

## Features

- One icon (keyboard, mouse, headset, headphones, earbuds, gamepad) and percentage per device, inside the taskbar next to the clock or on the left side, on any monitor, with an optional offset.
- Lightning bolt while charging; level turns red below a chosen low-battery threshold.
- Hides with the taskbar in full-screen apps and auto-hide; follows Windows light/dark mode.
- Settings window with a live preview: show/hide, reorder, relabel and pick the icon per device; text size; compact two-row mode; poll interval.
- Disconnected devices hidden (or shown dimmed). Short name tags only when two devices share an icon.
- Optional update check against GitHub releases; updates install only on click and are verified against SHA256SUMS.txt.
- Includes `wbt.exe`, a command-line tool that prints every battery once (`wbt --json` for JSON).
- Settings file: `%APPDATA%\wireless-battery-tray\config.toml`.

## Supported devices

| Device / family | Connection | Battery | Charging |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bluetooth headsets, earbuds and other devices that report battery to Windows | Bluetooth classic | yes | no |
| BLE keyboards and mice (GATT Battery Service), including both halves of split keyboards | Bluetooth LE | yes | no |
| Logitech devices on Unifying, Bolt and Lightspeed receivers (HID++ 2.0, works alongside Logi Options+) | 2.4 GHz receiver | yes | yes |
| SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 family | 2.4 GHz dongle | yes | yes |
| Sony DualShock 4 | Bluetooth, USB | yes | yes |
| Keychron keyboards on a Keychron Link receiver | 2.4 GHz receiver | no (listed as connected only) | no |

## Known limitations

- Keychron keyboards over 2.4 GHz report no battery through the Keychron Link receiver; in Bluetooth mode they work.
- Logitech MX Master 3 reports no level while charging, so only the charging bolt shows.
- ZMK split keyboards show only the central half unless built with `CONFIG_ZMK_SPLIT_BLE_CENTRAL_BATTERY_LEVEL_PROXY=y` and `CONFIG_ZMK_SPLIT_BLE_CENTRAL_BATTERY_LEVEL_FETCHING=y`.
- SteelSeries Arctis on older firmware reports in 25% steps; DualShock 4 in 10% steps.
- Not code-signed yet: Windows SmartScreen may warn; choose More info, then Run anyway.
